title: Welcome to Atlas
body:
Your team’s knowledge, all in one place.

Use this space to find answers, share what you know, and keep everyone moving in the same direction.

Getting your bearings
Start by exploring your team’s spaces. Each space brings related documents together, from onboarding guides to technical references.

Make yourself at home
Search for a topic, browse a space, or ask an administrator to add something you need. Keep documents focused, helpful, and easy to find.

title: Your first week: the onboarding guide
body:
Welcome to the team! This guide will help you settle in and get ready for your first week.

Day one
Meet your teammates, set up your accounts, and get familiar with our tools.

This week
Schedule an introduction with your manager. Browse the team handbook and learn how we work together.

Need a hand?
Reach out to your manager if you need help getting access to a workspace.

title: Engineering handbook
body:
A shared reference for how we build and maintain our products.

Our principles
Keep changes small and reviewable. Write clear documentation. Prefer simple solutions that are easy to maintain.

Development workflow
Create a branch for your work, include meaningful tests, and request a review before merging.

Releases
Verify changes in a staging environment and document any operational considerations.

title: Design system foundations
body:
Our design foundations help us create a consistent product experience.

Typography
Use a clear hierarchy and readable text sizes. Keep interface language concise and helpful.

Color and accessibility
Use color with purpose. Always pair status colors with text labels and maintain readable contrast.

Components
Build with reusable components and document new patterns as they emerge.

title: How we work together
body:
Our working agreements are a starting point for thoughtful collaboration.

Communicate clearly
Share context, make decisions visible, and document what others will need later.

Protect focus time
Use asynchronous updates when possible. Give meetings a clear purpose and an agenda.

Keep learning
Ask questions, share feedback, and make time to improve how we work.

title: Writing great documentation
body:
Good documentation helps someone take their next step.

Start with the reader
Explain what the document is for and who will find it useful.

Make it scannable
Use short paragraphs, descriptive titles, and practical examples.

Keep it current
Review documents when workflows change. Archive or update outdated instructions.
